messages:
jane-support: customer reported big p95 jump from APAC (~850ms) starting ~06:30 UTC. they pasted a trace where request goes ap-sg-edge -> us-east-1 -> eu-west-1 -> app. they think routing is wrong, asked for help.

kevin-netops: can you drop the trace id and a sample request headers? curious if region-hint/header present or if our affinity timed out.

jane-support: trace id trace-20260318-9a7. sample trace excerpt: ```span0 ingress ap-sg-edge -> span1 proxy us-east-1 -> span2 nat eu-west-1 -> span3 app-us-west-2``` no X-Region-Hint in headers. client IP is in SG, customer expects ap-southeast-1 region.

matt-infra: quick check — what does our routing policy say for ap-sg? run `rdw-route inspect ap-sg-edge --json` but easiest repro: `curl -H "Host: api.redwood.example" -H "X-Forwarded-For: 203.116.0.12" https://api.redwood.example/v1/ping -v` to see which edge we land on. also try `-H 'X-Region-Hint: ap-southeast-1'` to force.

kevin-netops: ran a tracewalk against that trace id, output snippet: ```rdw-trace trace-20260318-9a7 --path
1 ap-sg-edge (edge-3)
2 us-east-1-proxy (global-pool-12)
3 eu-west-1-nat (egress-7)
4 app-us-west-2
``` looks like global-pool fallback took the request from ap-sg-edge to us-east-1 then it hopped to eu-west-1 egress before reaching app. suspect affinity timeout / pool selection rule.

tracing-bot: auto-insight: high prefix-miss rate on ap-sg edge between 06:25-06:40 UTC. KV prefix cache miss -> routed to global pool. see rule id: routing.fallback.globalPool.v3.

lisa-eng: did we change fallback policy recently? I remember a tuning run this morning to reduce sticky affinity TTL for burst spread.

kevin-netops: confirmed — PR #4521 merged at 05:58 UTC reduced region-affinity TTL from 60s -> 5s to improve balancing. that would increase chances of immediate fallback to global pool when requests are bursty. rolling back to 60s should reduce cross-region hops.

jane-support: can we get a quick mitigation we can ask the customer to test while we rollback? suggested repro curl with header: ```curl -H "X-Region-Hint: ap-southeast-1" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'``` tell them to verify `x-rw-edge-region` response header.

matt-infra: starting rollback of routing.fallback.globalPool.v3 -> reverting TTL to 60s now. will patch config across edges.

deploy-bot: deploy started: config-revert routing.fallback.globalPool.v3 by matt-infra at 06:57 UTC. 12/12 edges patched.

kevin-netops: confirm post-rollback trace for same customer ip: ```rdw-trace trace-20260319-repro --path
1 ap-sg-edge (edge-3)
2 app-ap-south-1 (local-pool-5)
``` no trans-ocean hop.

jane-support: customer ran the header test and low-latency restored (p95 ~40ms). customer says things look normal again. closing the escalation. :thumbsup:
